Kubernetes client configuration

Source: R/configuration.R
Configuration.Rd

Kubernetes client configuration

Kubernetes client configuration

Details

A transport + authentication bundle. Populated by load_kube_config() or load_incluster_config(), or constructed directly for tests.

Mirrors kubernetes.client.Configuration from the Python client and the rest.Config struct from client-go.

Public fields

host

API server URL (e.g. "https://10.0.0.1:6443").

api_key

Named list of API-key-style headers, e.g. list(authorization = "Bearer ...").

username

HTTP basic auth username.

password

HTTP basic auth password.

ssl_ca_cert

Path to a PEM CA bundle.

cert_file

Path to a PEM client cert.

key_file

Path to the PEM client key.

verify_ssl

Verify server TLS certs (logical).

proxy

Optional proxy URL.

user_agent

User-Agent header.

exec

Optional list(command, args, env, apiVersion) exec plugin.

token_file

Optional path to a file holding a bearer token (reread on each request to handle rotation - matches in-cluster behaviour).

context_name

Name of the kubeconfig context used, for reference.

timeout

Optional per-request timeout in seconds for ordinary (non-streaming) calls. Watches and log streams are not affected.

max_retries

How many times ordinary requests are retried on HTTP 429 (any method, honouring Retry-After) and, for GET/HEAD, on 500/502/503/504 or connection failures, with jittered exponential backoff. 0 disables retries.

namespace

Default namespace from the kubeconfig context (or the in-cluster service account), or NULL.

tls_server_name

Server name to use for TLS SNI and certificate verification instead of the host in host (kubeconfig tls-server-name).

auth_provider

OIDC auth-provider settings from the kubeconfig (list(name = "oidc", config = ...)), or NULL.

exec_cluster

Cluster details handed to an exec plugin that sets provideClusterInfo: true (filled in by load_kube_config()).

Method new()

Construct a Configuration. All arguments are optional.

Usage

Configuration$new(
  host = NULL,
  api_key = NULL,
  username = NULL,
  password = NULL,
  ssl_ca_cert = NULL,
  cert_file = NULL,
  key_file = NULL,
  verify_ssl = TRUE,
  proxy = NULL,
  user_agent = "rk8s/0.2.0",
  exec = NULL,
  token_file = NULL,
  context_name = NULL,
  timeout = NULL
)

Arguments

host, api_key, username, password, ssl_ca_cert, cert_file, key_file

See fields of the same name.

verify_ssl, proxy, user_agent, exec, token_file, context_name, timeout

Likewise.

Method bearer_token()

Return the current bearer token, refreshing via the exec plugin or token file if configured.

Usage

Configuration$bearer_token()

Method client_cert()

Client certificate and key files to present, if any. An exec plugin that returns a certificate takes precedence over cert_file/key_file.

Usage

Configuration$client_cert()

Returns

list(cert_file, key_file); elements may be NULL.

Method refresh_credentials()

Drop cached exec-plugin credentials so the next request runs the plugin again (called automatically on HTTP 401).

Usage

Configuration$refresh_credentials()

Method clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

Usage

Configuration$clone(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.

Examples

# In-memory config - typical tests or ad-hoc use against a known endpoint.
cfg <- Configuration$new(
  host = "https://10.0.0.1:6443",
  api_key = list(authorization = "Bearer <token>"),
  verify_ssl = FALSE
)
cfg$bearer_token()
#> [1] "<token>"
